judged_text: saveChanges fires embedding.update({}) as a dropped promise (no .then/.catch) against an update endpoint that persists nothing — Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders the current state — and no template in this diff wires the action to any button. The next maintainer who wires this action up (the method name and the PUT /admin/customize/embedding route advertise a save) ships a button that reports success while saving nothing, and a failed PUT is swallowed without any error surfaced to the user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an Ember controller action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` without any `.then/.catch` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), and it also adds a PUT route/controller action `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` that does not persist anything and simply re-serializes the current `@embedding` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb). Additionally, the new `embedding.hbs` template wires only `addHost`/`deleteHost` and contains no button invoking `saveChanges`. So it’s not a user-facing broken behavior in this diff, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/footgun issue: the presence of a “save” action and PUT endpoint suggests saving should occur while it currently does not and errors would be unhandled if wired up later.
